paper_title: MMAR A Challenging Benchmark for Deep Reasoning in Speech, Audio,   Music, and Their Mix
caption: : Task Taxonomy
model_annotation: This radial chart, titled “Task Taxonomy,” visually organizes a set of analytical tasks into three concentric layers, each representing a different level of analysis: the innermost “Perception Layer” (40.4%), the middle “Semantic Layer” (41.2%), and the outermost “Content Analysis” (18.4%). The Perception Layer, colored dark blue, includes tasks such as Music Theory, Counting & Statistics, Environmental Perception & Reasoning, Correlation Analysis, Temporal Analysis, and Spatial Analysis. The Semantic Layer, in a lighter blue, encompasses Emotion & Intention, Speaker Analysis, and Content Analysis. The outermost Content Analysis layer, also in light blue, contains tasks like Professional Knowl & Reasoning, Culture of Speaker, Imagination, Acoustic Quality Analysis, Anomaly Detection, and Audio Difference Analysis. Each task is labeled with its name and, where applicable, its percentage contribution to the respective layer. The chart features a legend-like structure with distinct color coding for each layer, and the segments are arranged in a circular, descending order by size within each layer, though no explicit legend or percentage labels are shown inside individual slices beyond the layer totals.
